author: Iván Felipe Benavides-Martínez, Justin Guthrie, Jhon Edwin Arias, Yeison Alberto Garcés-Gómez, Ángela Inés Guzmán-Alvis, Cristiam Victoriano Portilla-Cabrera, Somnath Mondal, Andrew J. Allyn, Auroop R. Ganguly

title: DAAC: Deep Autoencoder-Based Aerosol Clustering From Ground-Based Remote Sensing and Its Evaluation at a Global Scale
content: Atmospheric aerosols remain a major source of uncertainty in Earth system modeling, and their classification using AErosol RObotic NETwork (AERONET) data is challenging. Fixed thresholds oversimplify mixtures, supervised approaches lack labels, and unsupervised methods miss rare aerosol regimes. This study proposes a deep autoencoder-based aerosol clustering (DAAC) framework. An autoencoder that captures inherent nonlinear relationships in aerosol optical properties and creates a compact and physically meaningful latent representation. Further, clustering is subsequently performed in the latent space to enable improved separability and compactness. The DAAC framework is evaluated on AERONET V3 data ( $4.81 {\,}\times {\,}10^{5}$  observations, 139 sites) and demonstrates consistent improvements in cluster separability across global regions compared to classical clustering methods. Improved scores in the Silhouette are observed, increasing from 0.44 to 0.78 in North America, 0.40–0.69 in South Asia, 0.31–0.53 in East Asia, and 0.35–0.55 in Europe. More moderate yet consistent improvements are evident in Africa 0.68–0.75, South America 0.34–0.397, and Australia 0.33–0.38, reflecting enhanced clustering performance under varying levels of aerosol complexity. In general, the framework provides a scalable and geographically transferable solution for aerosol regime clustering.
author: Varsha Pravin Hole, Manu Mehta, Subhash Shinde, Aaditya Sawant

title: DGAFNet: A Dual-Branch Gradually Cross-Attention Fusion Network for Precipitation Nowcasting
content: Short-term precipitation forecasting is critical for transportation, agriculture, and disaster management, where accurate and timely predictions can significantly reduce risks and improve decision-making. However, traditional methods such as numerical weather prediction (NWP) and radar echo extrapolation often fail to capture fine-grained spatiotemporal dynamics, especially under high-intensity precipitation. To alleviate this issue, we propose a dual-branch gradually cross-attention fusion network (DGAFNet) based on locality-aware SwinLSTM (LASL), which fully captures the spatiotemporal evolution of precipitation by integrating multisource data from radar and satellite observations. In DGAFNet, the satellite branch is tailored to model global–local spatial dependencies, while the radar branch is specifically designed to exploit multiscale features by utilizing atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP). In addition, we introduce a gradually cross-attention fusion module (GCAFM), which leverages attention mechanisms to adaptively highlight key informative regions and dynamically merges features from the dual branches at multiple levels. Experimental results on the storm event imagery (SEVIR) dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art models (ConvLSTM, PredRNN++, SwinLSTM-B and CM-STJointNet) across metrics, especially under high-intensity precipitation scenarios. These results highlight DGAFNets ability to effectively combine multisource data for more accurate and timely precipitation forecasting.
author: Haofeng Jiang, Yongfang Wang, Yanqing Zhang

title: Land–Ocean Transfer Learning for Global 1-arc-second DEM Super-Resolution
content: High-resolution (HR) global digital elevation models (DEMs) are essential for coastal and marine research, yet publicly available global bathymetric DEMs remain limited to 15-arc-second resolution. Producing a seamless 1-arc-second global DEM is challenging because HR marine DEM data are scarce and low-resolution (LR)-HR DEM pairs often come from different elevation products. Unlike prior DEM super-resolution studies focused on regional or synthetic degradation settings, we formulate global land–ocean reconstruction as real cross-product super-resolution and propose global super-resolution digital elevation model (GSDEM), integrating land–ocean transfer learning with a Swin Transformer backbone, SimpleGate-based feed-forward design, and cascaded  $\times 3$  followed by  $\times 5$  reconstruction. GSDEM is pretrained on large-scale terrestrial DEMs and fine-tuned on coastal and marine DEMs to transfer terrain knowledge from land to ocean. Compared with marine-only training, land–ocean transfer learning reduces mean root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and Slope RMSE by 18%, 19%, and 20%, respectively. Across ten spatially independent test regions, GSDEM achieves the lowest RMSE in all cases. Compared with representative convolutional neural network (CNN), generative adversarial network (GAN), and Transformer-based learning baselines, GSDEM reduces average RMSE, MAE, and Slope RMSE by 9%, 11%, and 12%, respectively, improves peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) by up to 2.9 dB, and increases mean structural similarity index (SSIM) to 0.9985. Applying GSDEM to GEBCO 2025 generates global land-ocean digital elevation model (GLOD)-1s, a seamless global 1-arc-second land–ocean DEM of about 2.4 TB. ICESat-2 ATL24 validation yields an overall RMSE of 2.75 m, and national centers for environmental information (NCEI) trackline-based checks support stable deep-ocean reconstruction. GLOD-1s provides an HR elevation baseline for global coastal and marine applications.
author: Chaofan Yang, Chenhao Wu, Mingjun Yang, Bo Zhang, Danfeng Hong, Meng Zhang, Qi Wang, Xiaomeng Huang, Chenhu Huang, Haifeng Zhang

title: Fast and Accurate Inversion Method of Asteroid Physical Parameters With a Lycaon Pictus Hunting Algorithm
content: The inversion of physical parameters of asteroids is a core technology for planetary exploration engineering. There are two key limitations to traditional approaches: the objective function is nearly flat in certain parameter subspaces, making the corresponding chi-square values almost identical, while exhaustive sampling over the entire parameter space incurs prohibitive computational costs. To address these issues, we propose weakly observable subspace theory, which proves the existence of a weakly observable subspace in the parameter space where the objective function is approximately flat, making it difficult to distinguish physical parameter vectors of asteroids with high errors. Under the guidance of this theory, we propose a fast and accurate inversion method with a Lycaon pictus hunting algorithm (LPHA). This approach is inspired by two unique hunting mechanisms of Lycaon pictus, including region lock and roaming hunt. In region lock, we use singular value decomposition (SVD) of high-order derivative information and the Hessian matrix to estimate the weakly observable subspace, which is locked as the hunting region. In roaming hunt, we perform concentrated sampling in that subspace followed by Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) refinement. This framework provides mathematical characterization of the weakly observable subspace and translates biological hunting into a sampling scheme, reducing unnecessary Monte Carlo (MC) samples. Simulation results on multiple asteroids demonstrate that LPHA achieves over 60% reduction in estimation errors while requiring only 10.13% of the computation time of the conventional LM approach. LPHA provides a fast, accurate, and theoretically grounded solution for asteroid physical parameter inversion, with broad applicability to other high-dimensional nonlinear inverse problems.
author: Yangyang Li, Jin Liu, Zhiwei Kang, Xiaolin Ning, Xin Ma, Jiancheng Fang

title: ChangeMix: Change-Aware Cut-and-Paste Augmentation for Semisupervised Remote Sensing Building Change Detection
content: Remote sensing change detection (CD) underpins applications such as urban monitoring and disaster assessment. However, performance is often constrained by scarce pixel-level annotations and by severe class imbalance, where unchanged pixels vastly outnumber changed ones. To address these challenges, we introduce ChangeMix, a change-aware cut-and-paste augmentation for semisupervised CD (SSCD) that dynamically constructs an instance bank of change regions from both scarce ground truth and high-confidence pseudolabels. ChangeMix stores paired prechange and postchange image crops, including their corresponding change and confidence masks, and pastes multiple instances onto strongly augmented unlabeled image pairs for class-balanced self-training. Furthermore, by randomly swapping the temporal order of the prechange and postchange patches before pasting, we vary the imaging conditions under which the pasted changes appear and keep appearance and disappearance events balanced. To demonstrate its applicability to building CD, we validated ChangeMix as a framework- and model-agnostic module. We integrated it into three distinct semisupervised learning (SSL) frameworks (FixMatch, UniMatch V1, and UniMatch V2) and tested it across multiple network architectures (DPT with DINOv2 backbones and DeepLabV3+). Extensive experiments show consistent improvements across the benchmarks. At the 20% label budget with the dense prediction Transformer (DPT)/DINOv2-Base architecture, averaged over three random seeds, ChangeMix increases changed-class intersection-over-union by 0.58–0.85 points on LEVIR-CD and 0.91–1.29 points on WHU-CD across the three frameworks. ChangeMix provides a practical and effective tool that can complement existing semisupervised pipelines to address critical data-related challenges in remote sensing. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/IonutMotoi/ChangeMix
author: Ionut M. Motoi, Wei Huang, Thomas A. Ciarfuglia, Daniele Nardi, Xiao Xiang Zhu

title: Dual-Patch Physical Adversarial Attack Against Localization Capability of Aerial Object Detection Based on Grid-Anchored Neuron Activation
content: In recent years, physical adversarial attacks against aerial image object detectors have attracted increasing attention. However, attacking the localization capability remains underexplored for physical adversarial attacks, and the simultaneous suppression and generation objectives can exhibit competing optimization directions between suppressing the feature response of the ground-truth object and inducing high-confidence responses at a targeted background region. To alleviate these issues, this article proposes a dual-patch physical adversarial attack (DPPAA) method to attack the localization capability of aerial object detectors. Specifically, the contradictory adversarial objectives are disentangled into two modules: a suppression module to suppress the confidence and an enhancement module to induce high-confidence activations at a targeted background region. GANA maps phantom geometry to detector-native responsible prediction units, including grid/anchor units in anchor-based detectors, to activate the corresponding prediction heads. Furthermore, a synergistic optimization strategy incorporates decoupled total variation (TV) regularization and context-aware spatial constraints to improve texture smoothness and confine the patches to background regions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show strong localization-attack performance and measurable transferability across the evaluated detectors.
author: Sijun Guo, Hao Li, Kelin Dang, Maoguo Gong, Yue Wu, Yu Zhou

title: SGHFNet: A Saliency-Guided High-Frequency Enhancement Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Transformer-based methods have achieved promising results in infrared small target detection (IRSTD) by capturing global context and long-range spatial dependencies. However, unconstrained global interactions may weaken the responses of dim, low-contrast targets. Moreover, modeling only in the spatial domain makes it difficult to distinguish true targets from target-like noise and structured background clutter. These limitations can lead to false alarms and missed detections in complex infrared scenes. To address these challenges, we propose a saliency-guided high-frequency enhancement network (SGHFNet), which inserts a saliency-guided global fusion (SGGF) block into the encoder–decoder skip connections. The SGGF block comprises two components: 1) saliency-guided cross-attention (SGCA) introduces a saliency-guided bias to regulate cross-level channel interactions and preserve weak target responses and 2) spectral-gated feed-forward network (SGFFN) combines multiscale depthwise convolution with adaptive high-pass filtering (AHPF) to enhance target boundaries and local structures. Experiments on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K show that SGHFNet achieves competitive performance compared with 19 representative methods. Ablation studies further show that SGCA and SGFFN provide complementary gains in target recovery and false-alarm control.
author: Pei Zhao, Yuan Tai, Erbo Zou, Bo Lei

title: Physics-Informed Adaptive Neural Networks for Long-Term Land Surface Temperature Evolution
content: Accurate long-term spatiotemporal projections of urban land surface temperature (LST) are essential for tackling global climate change and developing resilient urban planning strategies. However, the mechanisms underlying the persistent increase in urban LST under global warming remain unclear. Using Xiamen, a coastal city with a distinctive mountain–city–sea spatial pattern, as a case study, we propose Phys-KANet—a long-term spatiotemporal simulation framework that combines physics-informed constraints with Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) to project the evolution of the urban thermal environment from 2024 to 2050. This framework specifically uses a convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) to capture temporal persistence in LST changes and integrates KAN to improve high-order nonlinear feature interactions and the fusion of 12 key driving factors. To encourage physically plausible long-term extrapolation, a physics-informed loss function (PINN-Loss) is incorporated by combining spatial-continuity regularization, vegetation–temperature consistency, and an energy-balance-inspired ecothermodynamic soft constraint. Extensive experiments show that Phys-KANet outperforms the evaluated spatiotemporal baselines in both prediction accuracy and spatial physical consistency. Based on the projected urban thermal evolution from 2024 to 2050, this study highlights the primary factors driving future temperature increases in Xiamen. The proposed method not only supports climate adaptation strategies in densely populated coastal cities but also provides a modeling framework for high-resolution long-term urban thermal-environment analysis and climate-resilient planning.
author: Tingting Hong, Hanyu Lin, Xiaotong Xu, Zhipeng Su, Yingying Wang, Min Yuan, Caipin Li, Jianyang Gao, Ruijiao Wu, Ruizeng Cai, Yixiong Zhang

title: CSNet: A Center-Surround Motion Saliency Integration Network for Moving Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Moving infrared small target detection in complex scenes remains challenging due to extremely small target size, low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR), and rapidly irregular motion across consecutive frames. Existing multiframe methods model motion association through implicit spatiotemporal correlation learning or explicit interframe alignment, but may entangle target motion with dynamic clutter and incur additional computational overhead. To address these limitations, we examine the multistage functional principle by which the biological visual system processes salient moving stimuli in cluttered dynamic scenes. In particular, we draw a functional analogy from the heterogeneous parallel processing at the retinal ganglion cell (RGC) layer to jointly modeling local saliency and interframe motion association in infrared sequences. Guided by this analogy, we propose a center-surround motion saliency integration network (CSNet) to integrate target-sensitive saliency responses according to cross-frame motion cues. Specifically, we construct a center-surround heteroscale detection (CSHD) module that draws inspiration from the context-conditioned response patterns elicited by different spatial stimulus configurations within the center-surround (CS) receptive fields (RFs) of RGCs, thereby enabling pixel-wise spatial saliency (SS) extraction. The motion saliency accumulation module (MSAM) then applies CSHD to target-reference feature pairs for motion-aware refinement and short-term response accumulation, yielding robust motion saliency (MS) representations. Subsequently, a spatial structure reconstruction decoder (SSRD) progressively organizes the MS representations into spatially coherent target predictions through coarse-to-fine multilevel integration. Extensive experiments on two public datasets (MIST and NUDT-MIRSDT) demonstrate that CSNet achieves a superior performance-efficiency tradeoff over existing methods. Compared to the previous state-of-the-art (SOTA) method, it reduces the parameter count and floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 31.76% and 45.11%, respectively. The code and model weights are available at https://github.com/Bo11anFu/CS-Net
author: Bohan Fu, Rui Gao, Zhengqin Xu, Yixiao Gu, Liang Chang, Dan Zeng

title: 3-D Precession Attitude Estimation for Space Targets Without Target Scale or Structural Priors via Dual-Satellite Micro-Doppler Collapse
content: The 3-D attitude inversion of noncooperative space targets is constrained by a heavy reliance on target scale or structure priors and the inherent noise sensitivity of time–frequency analyses. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes a dual-radar framework grounded in the micro-Doppler bandwidth collapse effect without requiring target scale or structural priors. Through rigorous mathematical derivation, we demonstrate that the line-of-sight (LOS) sweeping vector is orthogonal to the target’s precession axis at the global bandwidth minimum. This crucial geometric constraint enables deterministic 3-D axis estimation and decouples unknown target dimensions via an orthogonal-projection minimum mean square error (MMSE) model, achieving blind cone angle inversion. Extensive simulations validate the framework’s noise and sparsity robustness, enabling robust attitude inversion even under an extreme signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of −25 dB. Under a −20 dB SNR, the framework achieves a 3-D precession axis error of 0.62° and a cone angle error of 0.78°, further demonstrating generalized applicability for rigid-body targets. Finally, the failure boundaries and applicability limits of the proposed method are characterized. This research provides a novel perspective for the 3-D attitude inversion of space targets.
author: Tianqi Han, Xin Zhang, Jiahang Zhang, Yong Wang, Hongzhi Li

title: SAR-INR: SAR Imaging and Spatial-Variant Phase Error Compensation for Ship Targets via Implicit Neural Representation
content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging of maritime targets is of paramount importance. The echo data acquired under severe sea states exhibits complex space-variant phase errors, leading to severe defocusing in the reconstructed images. To address this challenge, this article introduces a novel paradigm for SAR ship imaging by proposing a self-supervised imaging and autofocusing framework, called SAR-implicit neural representation (INR). Rather than explicitly solving the objective function, the proposed method leverages INR to establish mapping relationships from spatial and temporal coordinates to both target scattering intensities and phase errors, thereby accomplishing the target image focusing task through a joint optimization framework. Specifically, two collaborative networks composed of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) are designed to establish the mapping relationships and parameterize the joint estimation of the imaging matrix and phase errors into network weights, incorporating high-frequency encoding to enhance the details of the reconstructed images. This method not only preserves the integrity of ship structures but also eliminates the severe memory bottlenecks associated with large-scale observation dictionaries. Furthermore, a progressive joint optimization scheme is proposed to guide the network training, obtaining focused SAR ship target images without the need for external paired data or the supervision of image-quality metrics. Experimental validations on both simulated and measured airborne SAR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in focusing performance, structural preservation, and background noise suppression.
author: Jiawei Huo, Qing Yang, Zhongyu Li, Junyan Li, Junjie Wu, Jianyu Yang

title: A Multi-Field-of-View Sea Surface Temperature Retrieval Model for Spaceborne Microwave Imager Nearshore Data
content: Accurate monitoring of nearshore sea surface temperature (SST) is crucial for coastal regions. However, the coarse spatial resolution of spaceborne microwave radiometers leads to contamination of nearshore observational fields of view (FOVs) by terrestrial radiation from adjacent land. This contamination causes abnormally elevated brightness temperatures (BTs), making precise SST retrieval challenging. This study proposes a nearshore multi-FOV SST (NMF-SST) retrieval model that uses a novel spatial-resolution enhancement mechanism. By constructing a multidimensional input parameter system integrating spatial correlation features from adjacent FOVs, the model establishes a mapping relationship between multi-FOV observations and nearshore SST. Experimental results based on the Fengyun-3D (FY3D) Microwave Radiation Imager (MWRI) data (within 60°S-60°N) show that the NMF-SST model significantly improves nearshore SST retrieval capability. The valid offshore distance for reliable retrieval is reduced from  $\ge $ 110 to  $\ge $ 20 km. Compared with SST data from the in situ SST Quality Monitor (iQuam) system (2023–2025), the model’s retrievals exhibited a bias of 0.12 K and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.13 K, achieving accuracy consistent with the MWRI SST product in open oceans. Furthermore, the model is also demonstrated to be applicable to open-ocean regions, where it achieves an RMSE reduction of approximately 20.8% compared with the single-FOV baseline. Overall, the proposed model not only provides a robust framework for spaceborne microwave SST retrieval but also offers a methodological reference for retrieving other ocean parameters, potentially enhancing the application of spaceborne microwave radiometers in coastal ecosystem monitoring and land–ocean interaction studies.
author: Zhou Zhang, Zhenzhan Wang, Xiaolin Tong

title: DPEE-STGAN: A Dual-Path Encoding-Embedded Style Transfer GAN for Multidomain Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
content: The spectral and radiometric characteristics of remote sensing imagery can vary substantially across sensors, geographic regions, and acquisition conditions, resulting in pronounced domain shifts. Consequently, semantic segmentation models trained on a source domain often suffer severe performance degradation when directly applied to heterogeneous target-domain imagery. To address this issue, we propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive segmentation framework based on image style transfer and introduce DPEE-STGAN, a dual-path encoding-embedded style transfer generative adversarial network (GAN). DPEE-STGAN separates style conditioning into an intrinsic path that preserves source-domain geometry and texture, and an extrinsic path that injects target-domain appearance cues through hierarchical structure and color control. The resulting pseudotarget images retain the source annotations and are used to fine-tune a source-pretrained segmentation model without target-domain labels. Experiments on heterogeneous uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) and satellite datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in both style transfer and cross-domain segmentation. DPEE-STGAN achieves the lowest source-referenced learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) among the compared methods in all six evaluated transfer settings. For Potsdam $\rightarrow $ Vaihingen and Vaihingen $\rightarrow $ Potsdam, the proposed framework reaches 72.85%/48.12% and 68.43%/40.27% in overall accuracy (OA)/mIoU, respectively, improving mIoU over the corresponding source-only baselines by 12.10 and 10.41 percentage points. Across 11 additional heterogeneous target domains, the mean building intersection over union (IoU) increases from 35.20% to 50.14%. These results show that explicitly decoupling source-content preservation from target-style injection provides an effective solution for semantic segmentation under substantial remote sensing domain shifts.
author: Baikai Sui, Chenxi Liu, Qingwang Wang, Zhen Zhang

title: Agent-Inspired Recurrent Control of Spectral-Composition Logits With Latent Condition Prototype Routing for Pansharpening
content: Pansharpening aims to reconstruct a high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) image from a low-resolution multispectral (MS) image and a high-resolution panchromatic (PAN) image. Although deep-learning-based methods have improved spatial–spectral representation, most still introduce PAN details through pixel-, residual-, or feature-level fusion, offering limited control over how spatial structures are assigned to spectral components. Many progressive methods also rely on repeated refinement blocks with limited adaptation to the current reconstruction state and refinement history. These limitations may cause detail misallocation, spectral distortion, or error accumulation under spatially varying PAN–MS observation mismatch. To address these limitations, we propose spectral-composition recurrent control for pansharpening (SCoRe-Pan), an agent-inspired recurrent control framework that recurrently updates spectral-composition logits, which describe pixel associations with learnable spectral components before normalization, and reconstructs the HRMS image through adaptive spectral-basis mixing. The recurrent controller follows a fully differentiable observation–history–condition–control procedure, integrating observation-state encoding, history memory (HM) retrieval, and stagewise control prediction, while condition prototype routing (CPR) adapts the update strategy to different PAN–MS observation states (OSs). Experiments on WorldView-II, QuickBird, and Maryland under reduced-resolution, full-resolution, cross-dataset generalization, robustness, ablation, and efficiency settings show that SCoRe-Pan achieves competitive or superior spatial–spectral reconstruction quality compared with representative traditional and deep-learning-based pansharpening methods. Our code can be found at https://github.com/Rui0913/SCoRe-Pan.
author: Rui Hao, Xin Jin, Puming Wang, Hongyue Huang, Cheng Xie, Qian Jiang

title: GIGCD: Gated Intergroup Contrastive Diffusion Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Diffusion models have demonstrated significant potential for hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) due to their powerful generative capabilities. However, existing diffusion-based methods typically employ a global screening mechanism across timesteps, which inadvertently filters out discriminative semantics along with noise. To address the issue, we propose a novel gated intergroup contrastive diffusion (GIGCD) framework for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, which aims to preserve and fully leverage discriminative multitimestep features. Specifically, we first propose a temporal-dynamic gating module (TDGM), which performs element-wise weighting via a gating mechanism following 1-D convolutions and generates a soft mask specific to each timestep to suppress noise while enhancing semantic representation. Then, considering the property that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) decreases as the diffusion timestep increases, we propose a structured grouping and aggregation module (SGAM). It partitions the multitimestep features in descending order of timesteps into three groups—structural, semantic, and detailed—to construct a structured intermediate feature, explicitly modeling intergroup relationships across different diffusion stages. Furthermore, we propose a dual-stage group enhancement module (DGEM) consisting of group interaction and group constraint. The former achieves the interactive fusion and enhancement of three feature groups through an attention-based graph topological structure, while the latter effectively constrains the information purity of the enhanced semantic feature groups through triplet-based contrastive learning. Extensive experiments on four public HSI datasets demonstrate that our GIGCD framework achieves superior classification performance, establishing state-of-the-art results on the Indian Pines (IP) and LK datasets with significant improvements in overall accuracy (OA), average accuracy (AA), and Kappa coefficient, while also yielding a marked gain in OA on the challenging Houston 2018 dataset.
author: Yuefeng Zhao, Zhongao Wang, Nannan Hu, Xianqi Meng, Yuning Ning, Siting Zhou

title: Bidirectional Cross-Task Mutual-Teaching for Few-Shot Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Semi-supervised few-shot hyperspectral image (HSI) classification (CLS) typically relies on homogeneous classifier collaboration, where knowledge exchange remains confined within the CLS task and is prone to confirmation bias from accumulated pseudolabel errors. To overcome this inherent limitation, we propose a Bidirectional Cross-Task Mutual-Teaching (Bi-CTMT) approach that establishes a fundamentally new collaborative paradigm, coupling a patch-level CLS stream with a region-level segmentation (SEG) stream for bidirectional heterogeneous task interaction, rather than conventional same-task classifier ensembling. The two streams maintain exponential moving average (EMA) teacher models to provide temporally stable cross-task soft supervision via reliability-aware Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence alignment, enabling the SEG stream to supply region-aware structural guidance for pixel-level discrimination and the CLS stream to offer fine-grained discriminative cues for dense prediction. To further ensure pseudolabel quality, we develop a multiconsistency-based pseudolabeling (MCPL) strategy that integrates distribution-guided spatial consistency (DGSC), spatial–spectral consistency refinement (SSCR), and cross-task label fusion, so that selected pseudo-labels simultaneously satisfy local discriminative reliability and regional structural coherence. Experiments on three benchmark HSI datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves stable and competitive CLS performance in label-scarce scenarios.
author: Hongwen Yu, Dongsheng Ren, Junjie Zhang, Guanyi Li, Yutao Rao, Yazhou Yao

title: WHU-Hi+: A Large-Scale Benchmark Dataset for Fine-Grained Hyperspectral Cross-Image Classification
content: High-spatial–high-spectral-resolution uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery provides detailed spectral–spatial information for fine-grained agricultural mapping, while existing hyperspectral benchmarks remain limited in spatial coverage, category complexity, and evaluation protocols. To address these limitations, we introduce WHU-Hi+, a large-scale UAV-based hyperspectral benchmark for fine-grained hyperspectral image classification. WHU-Hi+ represents a complex agricultural scene and comprises 105 nonoverlapping image tiles with 11 crop categories. The dataset is characterized by a fine-grained crop taxonomy, class imbalance, interclass spectral similarity and intraclass spectral variability, and heterogeneous crop distributions across image tiles. To support comprehensive evaluation, we establish three train–test partitioning protocols including random pixel sampling (Protocol A), within-tile label partitioning (Protocol B), and tile-disjoint partitioning (Protocol C). Protocol B uses entire tiles as inputs but restricts training supervision to one half of each tile, whereas Protocol C further restricts training inputs to designated training tiles, excluding test tiles entirely. Ten representative deep learning methods covering convolutional, Transformer-based, Mamba-based, hyperspectral-specific, and foundation-model architectures are systematically benchmarked. Most methods show high performance under conventional random sampling but substantial degradation under spatially separated settings, showing that benchmark performance depends on the adopted evaluation protocol. WHU-Hi+ provides a challenging benchmark for evaluating fine-grained hyperspectral image classification under diverse spatial partitioning settings. The dataset, protocols, and benchmark code are publicly available at the project website (https://jiangyuelin0615.github.io/WHU-HiPlus/)
author: Yuelin Jiang, Xinyu Wang, Yingyi Liu, Yunning Peng, Xin Hu, Yanfei Zhong

title: SFDA-Net: Spatial–Frequency Dual-Branch Autoencoder Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) aims to estimate endmember spectra and fractional abundances from mixed pixels and is a fundamental task in remote sensing image analysis. Despite recent advances in deep learning-based blind unmixing, three challenges remain. First, many convolutional unmixing networks rely primarily on local operations, which limits their ability to capture long-range spatial–spectral dependencies and broad spatial distribution patterns. Second, the global pooling used in some attention mechanisms may weaken pixel-level coordinate information, which is important for dense abundance estimation and the preservation of spatial structures. Third, topographic effects and nonuniform illumination cause spectral magnitude variations, which may bias abundance estimation when a single linear decoder is shared across pixels. To address these issues, we propose SFDA-Net, a spatial–frequency dual-branch autoencoder (AE) for HU. First, a dual-branch feature extraction module (DFEM) combines learnable frequency-dependent Fourier filtering with local spatial convolution. The frequency branch captures long-range spatial dependencies, whereas the spatial branch preserves local neighborhood structure. Second, a coordinate attention module (CAM) uses separate horizontal and vertical encodings to recalibrate features, thereby retaining coordinate information during feature aggregation. Third, an intensity decoupling strategy (IDS) uses scale-normalized spectra for encoder-side representation learning and restores the observed spectral norm before reconstruction in the original reflectance domain. Experiments on two simulated datasets and four real or physically rendered datasets indicate that SFDA-Net provides reliable endmember extraction and abundance estimation across the evaluated datasets.
author: Chen Ding, Rundong Liu, Yizhuo Dong, Pengfei Wan, Canyu Zhang, Wenqiang Hua, Song Yan, Lei Zhang, Wei Wei

title: A Sparsity-Driven Lightweight Generative Adversarial Network via Structural Channel Pruning for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
content: Recently, deep learning has become a dominant paradigm for hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD), providing enhanced feature representation capability and improved detection accuracy. However, these performance gains are often accompanied by larger parameter scales and higher computational costs. This trend poses substantial challenges for deployment on resource-constrained edge platforms. To address this problem, this article proposes a lightweight generative adversarial network (GAN) for efficient HAD. The proposed model learns representative background distributions from hyperspectral images and reconstructs a pure background through a generative adversarial framework. Anomalous targets are then detected by analyzing the residual differences between the original hyperspectral image and the generated background. To obtain a lightweight detector, L1 regularization and soft-threshold shrinkage (STS) are applied to batch normalization (BN) scaling factors to promote channel sparsity. Channels with scaling factors below the predefined threshold are structurally pruned, thereby suppressing redundant feature responses and further reducing the model complexity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces both the parameter count and computational cost by more than 90% while maintaining nearly unchanged detection accuracy.
author: Kun Yu, Tianming Zhan, Xiaobing Yu, Shangdong Zheng, Zhihui Wei, Zebin Wu

title: Semantic-Guided Visual Representation Construction for Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
content: Remote sensing image–text retrieval (RSITR) continues to face significant challenges in achieving precise cross-modal semantic correspondence. While contrastive language–image pretraining (CLIP)-based methods are effective at instance-level alignment, most of them construct visual representations independent of individual text queries and rely on pairwise contrastive supervision. Consequently, fixed image embeddings may mix query-relevant evidence with visual content unmentioned by the query, while the shared embedding space may exhibit geometric inconsistency. Such geometric inconsistency manifests as inconsistent neighborhood relationships at the local level and persistent directional discrepancies at the global level across modalities. To address these problems, we propose a semantic-guided geometry-aware alignment (SGGA) framework for RSITR, centered on query-conditioned visual representation construction and further enhanced by local and global geometric regularization. Central to SGGA is a semantic-guided patch aggregation (SGPA) module that uses the text embedding as a semantic query to dynamically aggregate patch-level visual features, producing a candidate-specific visual representation for each image–text pair. To further regulate the geometry of the resulting query-conditioned embedding space, we design bidirectional neighborhood distribution alignment (BNDA) and shared anchor direction regularization (SADR) to preserve local neighborhood consistency and reduce global directional discrepancy across modalities, respectively. Furthermore, we design a gap-aware dual-query inference strategy that constructs complementary SGPA queries from the original sentence embedding and a gap-aware text centroid and fuses their similarity scores to improve retrieval robustness. Experiments on three RSITR datasets demonstrate that SGGA achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) retrieval performance.
author: Shen Ma, Jie Hui, Meiqin Liu, Jianji Wang

title: Prototype-Aware Reliable Target Structure Learning for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Remote Sensing Image Classification
content: Cross-domain few-shot image classification aims to learn transferable representations from a labeled source domain and enable few-shot recognition in a target domain. Recent studies improve cross-domain representation learning by incorporating unlabeled target data into semi-supervised training with labeled source data. However, most of them mainly exploit unlabeled target samples through prediction-level consistency, while lacking an explicit mechanism to organize target-domain samples into stable structural relations. This may lead to ambiguous feature distributions and unstable decision boundaries under large domain shifts. To address this issue, we propose prototype-aware reliable target structure (PARTS) learning, a framework for cross-domain few-shot remote-sensing (RS) image classification. PARTS consists of two complementary components: prototype-guided target structure learning (PTSL) and prototype reliability structure consolidation (PRSC). PTSL learns latent target-domain structures from unlabeled samples by organizing them through prototype-induced relations and refining their representations via prototype-guided residual adaptation. PRSC further consolidates the learned target structure by estimating prototype reliability and reducing redundancy among active prototypes. Together, the two components promote stable, compact, and discriminative target-domain representations under large domain shifts. Extensive experiments on multiple cross-domain RS benchmarks demonstrate that PARTS achieves competitive performance under both one-shot and five-shot settings.
author: He Wang, Yang Xu, Le Sun, Qixuan Wang, Zhihui Wei, Zebin Wu

title: Single-Point Supervised Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images via Joint Semantic and Structural Awareness
content: With the rapid advancement of oriented object detection (OOD) in remote sensing imagery, weakly supervised learning has shown great promise for reducing the costs of annotation. Among these, point-based supervision is the most efficient. However, the limited positional information from point labels makes it difficult to capture important target attributes, restricting the object detection accuracy. Focused on this, this article proposes an effective single-point supervised OOD network, in which category semantic information and structural edge prior are introduced. First, we design a semantic-guided point assignment strategy based on scarce single-point cues, aiming to drive the network to better predict angle and scale information via matching between instance targets and prior points. Specifically, class-wise semantic information derived from the forward inference process is used to construct a mask for selecting high-value prior points, which are then clustered with instance-level point labels as centers to optimize the precise assignment of prior points. Then, we further develop a multiscale attention mixture-of-experts (MS-Attn-MoEs) module to adaptively fuse multilayer feature maps for learning features of variable scales through a dynamic weighting mechanism. Moreover, a structure-guided Voronoi partition (SGVP) approach is presented, where a structure prior is primarily obtained through gradient computation, and then object shape estimation is refined to converge to the reference outline based on the Voronoi partition and segmentation results. Overall, the incorporation of semantic and structural prior knowledge can help to more accurately locate and classify objects with single-point supervision. Extensive experiments on public datasets validate the superiority of the proposed framework. The source code will be available at https://github.com/fan609/S2GPD
author: Yifan Xi, Ting Lu, Shutao Li

title: An Asymmetric Multitask Framework With Spatial Alignment and Gaussian Soft Detection-Oriented Fusion for Visible–Infrared Object Detection
content: The visible-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection is important for UAV perception under challenging conditions, such as low illumination, fog, and cross-modal spatial offsets. The existing RGB-IR detectors still face three coupled issues. First, the symmetric dual-stream backbones fuse visible and infrared features at all depths, although the deepest visible features are often unreliable under adverse imaging conditions. Second, the sensor differences and UAV viewpoint changes introduce residual spatial misalignment between modalities. Third, the common image fusion losses often suppress infrared–visible differences as reconstruction errors, rather than exploiting the thermal-appearance discrepancy to enhance detection-oriented target saliency while preserving context. To address these issues, we propose an asymmetric multitask framework for visible–infrared detection (VID-AMTF). The visible branch is truncated at res4, while the infrared branch preserves res5 as a reliable high-level semantic prior. A bilateral spatial aware module (BSAM) then predicts cross-guided deformable offsets and modulation masks for both modalities, performs depthwise feature alignment, and fuses features through an infrared-primary residual rule. In addition, a multimodal alignment loss (MAL) regularizes prefusion RGB/IR feature distributions, and a Gaussian soft detection-oriented fusion loss (S-DOFL) supervises an auxiliary decoder with Gaussian weights generated from ground-truth bounding boxes, selectively converting infrared-visible modality discrepancy into target-centric infrared saliency and visible-context preservation. The experiments on DroneVehicle and RGBT-Tiny show that VID-AMTF achieves strong detection performance and improves robustness under illumination degradation and spatial misalignment. The code will be released at https://github.com/KIKYOUWY/VID-AMTF
author: Yu Wan, Jie Li, Liupeng Lin, Yiliang Li, Yuzeng Chen, Zaiyan Zhang, Qiangqiang Yuan, Liangpei Zhang

title: HeteroAlloc: Content-Aware Heterogeneous Allocation for Remote Sensing Object Detection
content: Certain background regions in remote sensing images lack object-like structures, resulting in redundant computation in object detection. Existing coarse-to-fine methods focus on deep semantic discrimination between objects and background and thus fail to improve backbone efficiency at the early detection stage. To address this issue, we propose a content-aware adaptive computation allocation method that exploits statistical disparities in shallow features to reject regions clearly containing no objects at an early stage. Specifically, to overcome the challenge of indistinct semantic differences between targets and backgrounds in shallow-level features, we construct a set of complementary moment sampling (CMS) methods that enhance target–background discrimination by capturing subtle inter-channel distribution differences; to tackle label ambiguity arising from the lack of a strict definition regarding which regions should be rejected, we develop a sample similarity weighting mechanism that leverages neighborhood consistency in feature space, to mitigate the negative impact of ambiguous samples during training; moreover, to prevent the unintentional exclusion of critical targets, we design a closed-loop control strategy constrained by recall rate, maximizing background region elimination while guaranteeing target recall. Experiments on multiple remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the HeteroAlloc framework significantly reduces the computational overhead of various mainstream object detectors with minimal loss in accuracy.
author: Zhiyuan Deng, Wenzheng Wang, Zipeng Zhang, Yuqi Han, Haotian Sun, Mingzheng Mao, Chenwei Deng

title: Enhanced Denoising and Terrain Sample Densification of ICESat-2 Data Using a Bayesian Signal Model
content: The reliability of Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite (ICESat-2) terrain height retrieval depends heavily on effective photon denoising. However, uneven background noise often complicates conventional feature-based methods, leading to the erroneous rejection of crucial signal photons. To address this, this article introduces a Bayesian signal model (BSM) as a postprocessing framework designed to recover these misidentified photons and enhance ICESat-2/ATL08 photon-denoising accuracy, thereby increasing the number of reliable terrain height samples. The BSM innovatively leverages initial ATL08 outcomes to structure a K-nearest neighbor (KNN)-derived likelihood function, generating a robust heuristic normalized score for the retrieval of missed signal photons. Subsequently, this metric is applied within a sliding-window-based detection and refinement procedure, where the definitive identification of these missed signal photons is achieved via local Otsu thresholding constrained by ICESat-2 quality parameters to minimize the inclusion of true noise. Experimental results over large-scale regions demonstrate that, within the processing windows where the BSM performs signal recovery, the approach achieves an average overall Accuracy (OA) of 0.94, compared with 0.84 for the standard ATL08. Furthermore, after the adopted quality-control screening, the method substantially increases the density of valid terrain samples while maintaining vertical accuracy comparable to that of ATL08, validating the effectiveness of the BSM for large-scale geodetic control and digital elevation modeling. The reported denoising and terrain-retrieval metrics are therefore conditional on the adopted data-selection and quality-control procedures and should not be interpreted as global performance over the full range of ICESat-2 observations and conditions.
author: Zilong He, Zhiwei Li, Mi Jiang, Yushan Zhou, Chuwei Zhang, Xin He, Minzheng Mu, Chang Gu, Fukang Qiao, Yongze Song

title: Fast Asymptotic Modeling of Remote Acoustic Reflections From TTI Reflectors in VTI Boreholes: Monopole Excitation
content: Acoustic remote-reflection logging is widely used for characterizing geological structures surrounding boreholes, but in anisotropic formations, reflected-wave propagation exhibits strong directional dependence and mode-coupling effects, and conventional numerical simulations become computationally expensive for large-scale remote-detection problems. Existing asymptotic studies mainly focus on isotropic or simplified anisotropic models, leaving a gap in fast analytical methods for reflections from tilted transversely isotropic (TTI) interfaces received in vertically transversely isotropic (VTI) boreholes. To address this, a high-frequency asymptotic method based on generalized ray theory (GRT) and the method of steepest descent (MSD) is developed for remote reflections in VTI boreholes. Under far-field conditions, borehole radiation, interface reflection, and reflected-wave reentry are asymptotically treated via successive MSD approximations. GRT with Snell’s law determines the reflection path, yielding a compact frequency-domain formulation that requires only a single inverse Fourier transform to obtain transient responses. Finite-difference (FD) simulations validate the asymptotic solution at the waveform level for TTI formations, demonstrating good agreement in reflected-wave arrivals and waveform characteristics under representative anisotropic conditions. The method is applied to the Green River Formation to analyze remote reflection responses in realistic sedimentary environments.
author: Tian Lin, Jiaqi Xu, Hengshan Hu

title: Multiparameter Seismic Petrophysical Inversion Constrained by Rock Physics Modeling in Tight Sandstone Gas Reservoirs
content: Accurate estimation of petrophysical parameters is critical for characterizing tight sandstone gas reservoirs. However, the complex relationships between petrophysical attributes and frequency-dependent elastic behaviors pose considerable challenges to reliable seismic prediction. To tackle this problem, this study develops a rock-physics-constrained seismic petrophysical inversion framework for the quantitative estimation of multiple reservoir parameters. A key feature of the proposed method is the integration of a frequency-dependent rock physics model into the forward modeling operator of seismic inversion. This comprehensive model incorporates the effects of mineralogical composition, pore structure, and mixed fluid distribution, and computes low-frequency elastic properties to guarantee frequency consistency for seismic-band modeling. In addition, a model-based workflow is adopted to estimate microcrack porosity and fluid-patch parameters from well log data. These calibrated parameters, together with well-log-derived clay content, porosity, gas saturation, and permeability, are utilized to build initial models via Kriging extrapolation for Bayesian stochastic nonlinear inversion. Synthetic tests under both noise-free and noisy scenarios verify that the proposed method can reliably estimate petrophysical parameters, with inverted results consistent with the true models. Field seismic data applications further demonstrate that the inverted results match well with logging measurements. Overall, the integration of frequency-dependent rock physics modeling and Bayesian stochastic nonlinear inversion enables robust and quantitative multiparameter characterization of tight sandstone gas reservoirs.
author: Han Jin, Zhiqi Guo, Zhifang Yang, Danyu Zhao, Cai Liu

title: Seismic Random Noise Suppression in Angle-Domain Gather Using Phase-Reconstructed Deconvolutive Adaptive S-Transform
content: Random noise is a kind of irregular interference that widely exists in seismic data, and suppressing random noise can effectively improve the data quality, which in turn improves the accuracy of subsequent data processing and interpretation. Usually, the random noise in angle-domain gathers is randomly distributed, while the effective signals have certain similarity. To address this characteristic, we propose an adaptive time–frequency (TF) filtering method based on the phase-reconstructed deconvolutive adaptive S-transform (PDAST). The method first applies Lucy–Richardson deconvolution to the adaptive S-transform (AST) to enhance TF resolution, yielding the deconvolutive adaptive S-transform (DAST). It then estimates the phase information via weighted least squares, resulting in a PDAST representation that combines high resolution with invertibility. Leveraging the similarity of effective signals in the angle-domain gather within the TF domain, a 2-D TF filter is constructed through multitrace stacking and adaptive thresholding to effectively suppress random noise. TF analysis (TFA) on synthetic signals shows that the proposed DAST and PDAST achieve good resolution and noise robustness, and the phase estimated by PDAST allows signal reconstruction with an error below 1%. Denoising tests on synthetic models further demonstrate that the method can effectively suppress both full-band and finite-band random noise while preserving the effective signals to the greatest extent. Finally, the method is applied to field angle-stacked data for noise suppression followed by Teager–Kaiser energy attribute extraction. The results confirm its strong applicability and practicality.
author: Xuefeng Wu, Huixing Zhang, Bingshou He

title: Prestack Inverse Q Filtering Method Constrained by Reweighted Lp-Norm Regularization
content: Subsurface medium absorption causes seismic wave energy attenuation, waveform distortion, and bandwidth compression, which significantly degrade the resolution of seismic data. For prestack seismic data, stratigraphic absorption attenuation varies with wave propagation paths, further distorting amplitude variation with angle (AVA) response characteristics, reducing the lateral continuity of gathers, and further impairing high-accuracy prestack reservoir characterization. To address this issue, this article proposes a novel prestack seismic inverse  $Q$  filtering method based on reweighted Lp-norm regularization. First, we derive the forward modeling formula of prestack gathers in attenuative media under the horizontally layered medium assumption. Second, attenuation compensation is formulated as an inverse problem, and the Lp-norm regularization term is reweighted simultaneously. Finally, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMMs) is utilized to obtain the optimal solution to achieve attenuation compensation of prestack seismic data. Targeting the sparsity of reflection coefficients, the proposed method takes reflection coefficients as inversion compensation objectives. By combining a reweighting function with the Lp-norm sparsity constraint, a reweighting matrix is dynamically constructed during iterations to adaptively adjust the strength of sparsity regularization. This enables accurate capture of reflection features at stratigraphic interfaces and full exploitation of amplitude information carried by reflection coefficients, ultimately achieving high-precision seismic attenuation compensation. Numerical model tests and field applications demonstrate that, compared with poststack compensation and conventional L1-norm constrained inverse  $Q$  filtering, the proposed method effectively corrects amplitude and phase distortions and accurately recovers the AVA characteristics of prestack gathers. It achieves superior overall accuracy and noise robustness, and can furnish reliable data support for high-precision prestack seismic inversion and reservoir prediction.
author: Xin Huang, Dongyong Zhou, Linkun Shi, Xiaotao Wen, Bo Li

title: Clutter Suppression for Lunar Penetrating Radar via Blind Sparse Deconvolution With Spatial Regularization
content: The Chang’E-4 mission marks a milestone in space exploration since it was the first time that a human-made object ever soft landed on the far side of the Moon. The rover of the mission, Yutu-2, carries two ground-penetrating radar (GPR) systems designed to map the lunar subsurface and determine its dielectric properties. To that extent, various processing techniques have been suggested to enhance interpretation and increase the overall quality of the data. This article introduces a method for deriving the 2-D subsurface reflectivity series using blind sparse deconvolution (BSD) with spatial regularization. BSD increases the resolution of the radagram and provides a comparative assessment of the dielectric properties of different layers. The derived reflectivity series and source wavelet are then used to reconstruct the B-Scan, excluding any sources of noise and clutter that cannot be captured by the sparse model. This effectively suppresses clutter without compromising the amplitude and resolution of targets’ reflections. The proposed scheme is tested on both real and numerical data, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing the interpretation of the Chang’E-4 data, and demonstrating its broader value for planetary radar in general.
author: Iraklis Giannakis, Yi Xu, Yan Su, Feng Zhou, Antonios Giannopoulos

title: A Curvilinear-Grid Eikonal Framework for Passive Seismic Source Location in Anisotropic Media: Theory and Numerical Validation
content: The accurate localization of passive seismic sources is important for geophysical applications, such as reservoir characterization and seismic-hazard assessment. Traveltime-based location methods are widely used for this purpose, but their accuracy can be significantly affected by complex surface topography and seismic anisotropy, which alter seismic traveltimes and may lead to biased source parameters when these effects are neglected or inadequately represented. To address this issue, we develop a passive-source location framework based on a topography-dependent eikonal equation (TDEE) formulated for anisotropic media on boundary-conforming curvilinear grids. The hypocenter is determined by globally minimizing a station-pair double-difference (DD) traveltime objective function, in which the origin time is eliminated, and the origin time is subsequently estimated from the absolute-traveltime residuals with the hypocenter fixed. Synthetic experiments involving complex topography and anisotropy are conducted to evaluate the accuracy, computational performance, and sensitivity of the method to observational and modeling errors. The results show that the proposed framework provides accurate hypocenter and origin-time estimates under various model configurations, whereas neglecting topographic or anisotropic effects can produce systematic biases in the estimated source parameters. The proposed method provides an effective traveltime-based approach for passive-source location in complex topographic and anisotropic media.
author: Xiaole Zhou, Haiqiang Lan, Gaoshan Guo

title: A History-Aware Residual-Learning Framework for Enhancing SMAP Soil Moisture Retrieval Over Organic-Rich Tundra
content: Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) L-band retrievals often show less seasonal soil-moisture variation than field measurements in organic-rich tundra. Freeze–thaw state and organic-layer wetness change through the year, whereas the operational algorithm uses mostly static soil parameters. We introduce the composite shared latent dynamic feature (C-SLDF), a residual-learning method that summarizes the previous 365 days of surface temperature, SMAP SCA soil moisture, vegetation optical depth, and H- and V-polarized brightness temperatures into five predictors learned separately within each validation fold. We compare it with the Operational SMAP single-channel algorithm (SCA), a static random forest (RF), and calendar-seasonal, equal-weight 365-day, and fixed-window history RF baselines. All features and models use training data only. In rolling next-month validation, Operational SMAP SCA had $R^{2}=-0.055$ and RMSE = 0.131 m$^{3}$ m$^{-3}$, whereas Learned History C-SLDF achieved $R^{2}=0.548$ and RMSE = 0.086 m$^{3}$ m$^{-3}$. An analytical seasonal branch identified importance peaks near independently derived thaw and freeze windows. In leave-one-site-out testing, a spatial extension achieved $R^{2}=0.165$ and RMSE = 0.124 m$^{3}$ m$^{-3}$, but its site-block 95% interval for $R^{2}$ included zero. A secondary rolling test across four available years (16 thawed monthly blocks; 6873 observations) showed a smaller gain over Equal365 ($\Delta R^{2}=+0.017$; $\Delta$ RMSE = −0.0030 m$^{3}$ m$^{-3}$). Preceding microwave and thermal observations therefore add information beyond the annual calendar phase. Temporal enhancement was consistent; spatial and cross-regional transfer require broader validation.
author: Chang-Hwan Park, Ankur Desai, Jingyi Huang, Hyunglok Kim, Andreas Colliander

title: Thermophysical Properties of Mare Tranquillitatis on the Moon: Insights From MRM Data
content: Mare Tranquillitatis is one of the oldest maria, experiencing a long-lived thermal evolution history. This study employs microwave data from the Chang'e (CE)-2 microwave radiometer (MRM) to investigate the subsurface thermophysical characteristics of this region. To mitigate the effect of latitudinal variations found in mare, we applied two previously developed models: normalized brightness temperature (nTB) and effective brightness temperature difference (TBDeff). Based on these models, the novelty of this work lies in two aspects: first, a quantitative Pearson correlation analysis between TBDeff and TiO2 abundance across 27 mapped basaltic units, which yields correlation coefficients of 0.85 at 3.0 GHz and 0.87 at 37 GHz; and second, a multifrequency depth-stratified decomposition of controlling factors, including topography, regolith composition, and rock abundance (RA) influences. Through the integrated analysis, the principal findings are as follows: first, there exists a fundamental microwave difference within Mare Tranquillitatis, which is related to the large volcanic complex; second, the distribution of TBDeff is primarily controlled by variations in TiO2 abundance, revealing a positive correlation at different channels; third, the correlation between elevated microwave anomalies and high intracrater RA confirms the influence of blocky materials on local thermophysical properties. This study demonstrates the capability of CE-2 MRM data, aided by the nTB and TBDeff models, to decipher the complex processes shaping the lunar subsurface, thereby providing a robust framework for interpreting future lunar exploration data.
author: Liansheng Mei, Cai Liu, Roberto Bugiolacchi, Feng Zhang, Xuegang Dong, Yibo Meng, Zhihao Wei, Huanzhao Chi, Qin Wang

title: X-Shaped Multistage Spatial–Frequency Domain Information Fusion Network for Pansharpening
content: The pansharpening task aims to integrate low-spatial-resolution multispectral images with high-spatial-resolution panchromatic (PAN) images to obtain high-spatial-resolution multispectral (HRMS) images. Despite significant progress in deep learning-based pansharpening techniques, inherent limitations still constrain their performance: From the perspective of leveraging two modalities, most spatial–frequency domain approaches typically either process fixed-scale spatial and frequency information in single-branch networks or process each domain multiscale information separately in dual-branch networks, which lack a multistage strategy to integrate multiscale spatial–frequency domain information in dual-branch networks, leading to coarse-grained details in HRMS images. To this end, we propose a novel X-shaped multistage spatial–frequency domain information fusion network to employ dual-domain information sufficiently, named X-MSFN. Specifically, our network is equipped with three significant modules. For the purpose of effectively merging modalities in dual-domain, we customize a novel multistage information fusion module to progressively integrate multiscale information, thereby significantly enriching detail representation. Moreover, channelwise transformer block module further integrates multiscale features within X-shaped network, enhancing the spectral representation capability of PAN branch. Finally, we obtain texture-rich and fine-grained HRMS images through the granularity-adaptive fusion module, which achieves adaptive modulation of features. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate our superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
author: Zhuomao Li, Ying Li, Zhihao Li, Yikun Liu, Minghao Liu, Gongping Yang

title: Mapping and Explaining Rice Cropping Intensity From Sentinel-1 Time Series: A Structural-Causal Deep Learning Approach (DeepSEM) Across the Vietnamese Mekong Delta
content: Rice cropping intensity (RCI) governs seasonal food supply, yet operational satellite products largely stop at a binary rice/nonrice label and reveal little about why cropping decisions vary in space. This article maps annual RCI in four classes across the 13 provinces of the Vietnamese Mekong Delta and, within the same inference pass, quantifies the climatic pathways that shape it. A structural-causal deep learning model (DeepSEM) couples a Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) (VV/VH) encoder to CHIRPS rainfall and ERA5-Land temperature through a distributed-lag attention layer and a latent structural block. The model is trained on 5 × 5-pixel patches from a subset of provinces and then applied wall-to-wall at 10 m, under a 2 × 2 design that varies training-set composition and temporal window length (L = 20, 30). Overall accuracy reaches 0.93–0.96 in-domain and 0.84–0.92 under zero-shot transfer to provinces never seen during training. Delta-wide planted area departs from official statistics by $-$16.4% with a Spearman correlation of 0.962, improving on the reference map used for supervision ($-$21.2%; 25.1% mean absolute bias). Training-set composition dominates window length: at L = 20 it reduces mean absolute bias by 8.7 points, against 1.5–3.0 points for extending the window. Structural attribution assigns comparable shares to the autoregressive, SAR and climate pathways ($\approx$0.35/0.34/0.30) in three of four configurations. An input-channel ablation shows that the meteorological pathway raises in-domain accuracy by 2.9 points without improving zero-shot transfer, and that a SAR-only variant yields the smallest area bias ($-$12.5% against $-$17.1%): the climate channels earn their place by what they make measurable, not by what they add to accuracy.
author: Irwan Rahadi, Shahibul Ahyan, M. Marzuki, Baiq Ahda Razula Apriyeni, Muhammad Djamaluddin, Kertanah

title: Fusion Compressed Sensing: A Data Fusion Approach for Mitigating Information Loss in Distributed Millimeter-Wave Radar Systems
content: Distributed millimeter-wave radar sensing has attracted increasing attention due to its ability to provide complementary multiperspective observations in complex environments. However, information loss caused by clutter interference, radar cross-section fluctuation, and target occlusion can still degrade detection accuracy and reliability, particularly when prior information or temporal models are unavailable. To address this problem, this article proposes a signal-level data fusion approach, termed fusion compressed sensing (Fusion CS), for distributed millimeter-wave radar systems. Fusion CS constructs a registered composite observation without cross-node averaging while retaining node-dependent latent responses during sparse reconstruction. A visibility-gated structured sparsity regularization term is introduced to select visibility-consistent radar observations for ROI-level sparse support refinement, thereby reducing the influence of occlusion-induced low-signal-to-noise ratio or missing responses on the local structural prior. In the proposed framework, multiradar observations are registered into a common spatial representation, and ROI-assisted compression is employed to reduce the reconstruction dimension for efficient sparse fusion. Simulation and field-test results demonstrate that the proposed method improves target localization accuracy and reduces missed detections in distributed millimeter-wave radar sensing scenarios with partially missing information.
